title: Arch Manning addresses Steve Sarkisian-Holly Rowe interaction, sparks fresh criticism
content:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning joked Monday about an AI-altered video circulating on social media that depicted Steve Sarkisian slapping ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe, whom the Texas coach wouldn’t let ask a question during a brief interview after Saturday’s game against Ohio State.

Manning was asked whether he had seen any social posts from the postgame celebration of Texas’ 24-23 victory against Ohio State on Saturday night but was not asked directly about the Rowe-Sarkisian interview.

“I’ve seen a few AI edits, that’s about it. I saw an AI edit of Sark’s interview,” Manning said, drawing laughs from the room. “Y’all seen that one? That’s a good one. Of him slapping Holly Rowe. It’s hilarious.”

Sarkisian’s actual exchange with Rowe lasted less than five seconds after the Longhorns’ dramatic victory over Ohio State.

As those in burnt orange began celebrating the program’s fifth all-time win over a top-ranked opponent, Rowe attempted to begin her postgame interview with Sarkisian but couldn’t finish a question. Sarkisian interrupted her and screamed, “Let’s go, Texas fight! Let’s go, Texas fight!” into the microphone before adding “Hook ‘Em!” and walking off.

The broadcast’s halftime interview with Sarkisian also went awry, with cameras showing Sarkisian jogging up the stairs to the locker room as ESPN’s Laura Rutledge explained he had just left the field.

Rutledge eventually spoke with Sarkisian after Texas came out of the locker room to start the second half and clarified what happened as the teams were heading to the locker room at the break.

“I do want to make sure we clear something up: (Sarkisian) did decline the interview at the half,” Rutledge said before the start of the third quarter. “He had waited a long time, been very patient with some technical issues that we had. He apologized to us. We should be apologizing to him, which we did.”

A Texas spokesperson said Saturday night that ESPN’s technical difficulties arose once again on the field during the postgame celebration, which played a role in Sarkisian’s demeanor with Rowe.

The interview did not come up during Sarkisian’s regular Monday news conference, which took place before Manning took questions from reporters. The apparent flippancy of Manning’s exchange with reporters drew sharp responses online after the clip was posted to social media.

Neither Texas nor ESPN immediately responded to a request for comment Monday night.
